scope: Correct Jeremiah 31:32 disclosure and relocate its existing anchor; unchanged Hebrew and marker-free main English; source priority unresolved
note: Or, “though I was lord over them.” Greek Jeremiah 38:32 and Hebrews 8:9 instead have “and I disregarded them.” Whether this reflects another sense of the same Hebrew verb or a different Hebrew source remains disputed.
lexical_rationale: POB provisionally retains the covenantal husband metaphor; lord or master is another relational interpretation. Greek Jeremiah 38:32 and Hebrews 8:9 instead express disregard. A negative sense under the same Hebrew spelling has been proposed, but neither that interpretation nor a different Hebrew ancestor is established as earliest. The note distinguishes these alternatives rather than equating Greek disregard with dominion.
theological_rationale: Retain the husband interpretation provisionally while disclosing lord as an alternative and the Greek disregard wording separately. The relation between the Greek and Hebrew remains disputed; neither covenant theology nor the selected English settles historical source priority.
